new.s: Who is known as the 'Father of the Indian Space Programme'?
new.x: Dr Vikram Sarabhai (1919-71) is called the Father of the Indian Space Programme and was the first ISRO Chairman till his death in 1971. Homi Bhabha led the atomic energy programme (Sarabhai succeeded him at the AEC in 1966); Satish Dhawan was a later ISRO Chairman (1972-84); Kalam is linked with SLV-3 and missiles, not this title.

new.x: Annapurni Subramaniam is the 4th Indian and the first Indian woman to receive the COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal. She is not the first Indian, and not the second woman; the medal has been given since 1990, not instituted in 2026.
new.tq: COSPAR Sarabhai Medal (since 1990): 2026 = Annapurni Subramaniam, 4th Indian, 1st woman.

new.s: Cryogenic engines (liquid hydrogen + liquid oxygen) are mainly used in:
o: Military missiles kept ready for long periods
new.x: Cryogenic propulsion is used in rocket upper stages (and was used on the space shuttle) because of its very high specific impulse (~450 s). Its low-density LH2 needs huge tanks and cannot be stored long, so it is unsuited to military missiles; attitude-control thrusters use hypergolic propellants that ignite on contact; sounding rockets use solid motors.

new.s: The Indian National Satellite (INSAT) system is best described as a:
o: Combined communication and meteorological satellite system
new.x: INSAT serves both communication and meteorology from geostationary orbit (JPSC 2021 keyed it as a 'meteorological satellite'), and also carries broadcasting, disaster warning and search-and-rescue.
